第一个因素是接入型电子货币的欺诈风险。卖方或第三方可能获悉买方的账户信息，从而欺诈扣款，尤其是在互联网上。持有者也可能以欺诈方式在电子货币载体上增加货币单位。这两种欺诈一直是发行者、使用者和监管者高度关切的问题，因而有必要在加密技术方面投入大量资源。

The first is the risk of fraud attached to access e-money since the account details of the buyer might become known to the seller, or to a third party, thus allowing for fraudulent charging, especially over the internet. The holder might also fraudulently add units to e-money vehicles. Both types of fraud have been major concerns of access e-money issuers, users and regulators, thus necessitating substantial investment in encryption technology.
第二个因素是，大多数接入型电子货币会提供有关持有者的信息，尽管也有匿名形式。相比之下，银行券通常不会留下使用轨迹，因而适合非法交易和“灰色”交易。
银行券的匿名性也使使用者免受国家窥探。

The second is that most forms of access e-money provide information about holders, though anonymous forms also exist. In contrast, banknotes normally leave no trail of use, thus being suitable for illegal and ‘grey’ transactions.
Banknote anonymity also protects users against the attentions of a prying state.

第三个因素是，接入型电子货币处理极小额支付的能力有限。互联网足以说明其中的困难：建立一个可靠的电子货币“小额支付”（支付额只是记账单位的一小部分）系统，一直很不容易。使用接入型电子货币进行极小额购买会产生交易成本，使用麻烦本身就是一种成本，使得互联网使用者索性回避这类购买。在互联网之外，处理极小额支付时，铸币似乎优于接入型电子货币：方便携带，容易以足够小的面额供给，伪造所得微不足道，遗失的代价通常很小，生产及投放流通的成本也相对低廉。铸币可能是一种古老的货币形式，却仍然能在金融化资本主义的个人收入流通末端占主导地位。

The third is that access e-money has limited ability to deal with very small payments. The difficulties involved can be gauged from the internet where it has proven very difficult to introduce a reliable system of e-money ‘micropayments’ (a fraction of the unit of account). There are transactions costs – including plain inconvenience – to using access e-money for tiny purchases leading internet users simply to avoid the latter. Beyond the internet, coin appears to be superior to access e-money in dealing with very small payments: it is easy to carry; it can be readily supplied in sufficiently small denominations; there is negligible profit from counterfeiting it; the cost is generally small if it is lost; it is also relatively cheap to produce and to put in circulation. Coin might be an ancient form of money, but it is still capable of dominating the tail end of the circulation of personal income in financialised capitalism.
简言之，金融化时期，电子形式的信用货币开始主导流通，但银行券和铸币都没有因此过时，二者在个人收入循环和其他领域依然活跃。技术变化和与之相关的银行转型，支持了接入型电子货币的兴起。反过来，接入型电子货币影响了银行、产业资本和商业资本的运作，很可能也影响了它们的盈利能力。然而，同一时期还出现了另一种电子货币，它在质上有别于接入型电子货币，揭示了金融化的其他重要方面。

Electronic forms of credit money, in short, have come to dominate circulation in the years of financialisation, without rendering obsolete either banknotes or coin, both of which have remained robustly present in the circuits of personal income and elsewhere. Technological change and the associated transformation of banks have sustained the ascendancy of access e-money. In turn, access e-money has had an impact on the operations and probably the profitability of banks, industrial and commercial capital. During the same period, however, a further form of e-money has emerged which is qualitative different from access e-money and which reveals further important aspects of financialisation.

zh: 4.2 严格意义上的电子货币：金融化资本主义的一种新货币形式

children: E-Money Proper: A New Form of Money in Financialised Capitalism
严格意义上的电子货币是金融化过程中出现的一种新货币形式。简言之，它由私人发行，货币单位存储在电子设备上。购买者事先按面值支付普通货币换取这些单位，随后可以用它们购买发行者之外的其他主体所出售的商品。

E-money proper is a novel form of money that has emerged in the course of financialisation. Summarily put, it is money that is issued privately and its units are stored on an electronic device; units are purchased by advancing ordinary money at par value; the holder subsequently using these units to pay for commodities sold by agents other than the issuer.
这种电子货币中发展迅速的形式包括预付卡和在互联网上使用的预付软件程序，后者通常称为基于服务器的电子货币。
严格意义上的电子货币可以是“单功能”的，即只能在特定地点购买特定商品，例如百货商店卡与交通卡。也可以是“多功能”的，可用于更广泛的支付，例如所谓的智能卡或适用范围更广的交通卡。随着这种货币的普及，它可以与接入型电子货币共存于同一张卡上，即存储于银行借记卡或信用卡上。
Rapidly growing forms of e-money proper are prepaid cards, or prepaid software programmes used on the internet, often called server-based e-money.

E-money proper could be ‘single-function’, i.e. capable of buying particular commodities at particular locations, for instance, department store cards and transport cards. It could also be ‘multi-function’, allowing for a broader range of payments as, for instance, for so-called smartcards or transport cards with broader applications. As the use of e-money proper has spread, it has become possible to carry its units on the same card as access e-money, i.e. on bank debit and credit cards.

严格意义上的电子货币是发行者的负债，但在质上仍不同于普通信用货币，因而也不同于接入型电子货币。信用货币通常以债务为对应资产而发行，发行者以自身信用先行支付，持有者基于信任接受。信用货币的流动性一般高于发行者为此持有的资产。资产陆续到期时，发行者账上对应的信用货币负债也随之消除。相比之下，严格意义上的电子货币只能按面值用现成货币（通常是普通信用货币）购买。发行者可以将收到的资金作为普通存款存于其他金融机构，也可以用来购买金融资产。

E-money proper is a liability of the issuer, but nevertheless differs qualitatively from ordinary credit money (and thus from access e-money). Credit money is typically issued against debt, and entails advancing the credit of the issuer which the holder accepts on trust. Credit money is typically more liquid than the assets held by the issuer against it, and drains away from the issuer as these assets mature. In contrast, e-money proper could only be issued against ready money (typically ordinary credit money) at par. The issuer could either hold the received funds as regular deposits with other financial institutions, or use them to purchase financial assets.

实际上，严格意义上的电子货币的发行者从持有者那里获得信用，直至持有者把已发行的电子货币单位兑换回普通货币。与信用货币不同，严格意义上的电子货币只有兑换为普通货币，才会从发行者账上消除。这使发行者不得不保有大量普通货币储备，或持有能够迅速兑换为普通货币的金融资产。发行者通过取得超过此类电子货币发行和管理成本的资产收益而获利。值得注意的是，这种电子货币的“货币性”通常低于购买它所支付的普通货币，即流动性更低，这也使它有别于普通信用货币。但它的“货币性”具有特定的局部性质，从而在特定情形下更合持有者的需要，交通卡就是一例。

In effect, the issuers of e-money proper receive credit from its holders which lasts until the issued units of e-money are converted back into ordinary money by the holders. In contrast to credit money, e-money proper drains away from its issuer only when it is converted into ordinary money. The issuers are thus obliged to hold large reserves of ordinary money, or of financial assets that could be quickly converted into ordinary money. Issuers make a profit be earning a return on the assets exceeding the costs of issuing and managing the units of e-money proper. It is notable, and provides a further contrast with ordinary credit money, that e-money proper typically has less ‘moneyness’ than the ordinary money paid for it – it is less liquid. However, its ‘moneyness’ has a specific and local character which makes it preferable to the holder, for instance, in the case of transport cards.
严格意义上的电子货币的运作，在很大程度上由支撑它的监管框架决定，而框架自然因国家而异。

不过，某些共同的监管特点塑造了这种电子货币的性质。严格意义上的电子货币只能以普通货币（通常是信用货币）按面值购买，还必须按面值兑回。发行者须遵守严格的资本持有规定，只能投资于范围狭窄、流动性极高的证券，主要是公共金融资产。因此，监管使发行者无法像普通银行一样运作，因为他们不能以发行严格意义上的电子货币来发放贷款或购买证券。通常情形恰与银行相反：由于持有者必须预先支付现成货币才能取得这种电子货币，只要没有立即花出去，持有者就是在向发行者提供信用。
The functioning of e-money proper is substantially shaped by the regulatory framework supporting it, which naturally varies among countries.

However, certain features of regulation are held in common and have shaped the character of e-money proper. Thus, e-money proper could only be issued in exchange for ordinary (typically credit) money at par; it must also be redeemed at par; issuers face severe restrictions on the capital they must hold; issuers could only invest in a narrow range of very liquid securities – mostly public financial assets. Regulation, therefore, prevents issuers from operating as ordinary banks since e-money proper could not be issued to make loans or buy securities. The normal state of affairs is indeed the opposite of a bank: since the holder has to pay ready money to acquire e-money proper, as long as the latter is not immediately spent, the holder is giving credit to the issuer.

这一复杂的监管框架支持了人们对使用此类货币的信任，因而提高了它的可接受性。然而，严格意义上的电子货币在发达国家的普及程度有限，前文各图对货币流通所作的量化描述甚至没有提及它。普及有限还因为规定要求人们最初必须用普通货币按面值购买这种电子货币，这使它不适合企业间的大额交易。监管使它只能停留在小额货币的范围，主要在个人收入流通中充当交换手段和贮藏手段。在这个领域，既有货币形式的优势，尤其是银行券和铸币的优势，严重限制了它。

This complex regulatory framework has strengthened the acceptability of e-money proper by supporting trust in its use. Nonetheless, the spread of e-money proper has been limited in developed countries, not even meriting reference in the quantitative description of circulation in the figures given above. Limited spread is also due to the stipulation that e-money proper must be initially purchased at par with ordinary money, which makes it unsuitable for large transactions among enterprises. Regulation has forced e-money proper to remain small-scale money, functioning primarily as means of exchange and hoarding in the circulation of individual income. In that domain it has been heavily constrained by the strength of incumbent forms of money, particularly banknotes and coin.

概括说，严格意义上的电子货币在质上不同于信用货币，因为它并非来自信用的提供，而是用既有货币按面值换得的私人负债。它的出现是资本主义流通自发产生新货币形式这一内在趋势的实例。金融化时期，工商企业通过发行严格意义上的电子货币，使这一趋势重新加强。与此同时，在发达国家，这种货币仍局限于个人收入流通，未触及大额交易。监管和既有信用货币形式持续具有的优势限制了它的普及。不过，即使在这一点上，它的出现也反映了个人收入循环在金融化资本主义中的特殊重要性。

Recapping, e-money proper differs qualitatively from credit money since it does not emerge from the advance of credit but comprises private liabilities obtained in exchange for existing money at par. Its emergence is an instance of the inherent tendency of capitalist circulation spontaneously to generate new forms of money. In the years of financialisation, industrial and commercial enterprises have re-strengthened this tendency by issuing e-money proper. At the same time, in developed countries, e-money proper has remained confined to the circulation of personal income leaving large-scale transactions untouched. Regulation and the residual strength of incumbent forms of credit money have limited its spread. Even in this respect, however, the emergence of e-money proper has reflected the peculiar importance of the circuits of personal income in financialised capitalism.

值得注意的是，金融化资本主义内部的技术和制度变化所带来的自发创造货币的可能性，在发展中国家表现得更充分。严格意义上的电子货币在非洲和亚洲的一批国家兴起，尤其依托电信企业。在发展中国家，移动通信的普及为电子货币的可接受性及其“货币性”奠定了基础。通常，手机用户先支付普通货币购得这类电子货币，以电子单位持有，再通过简单的消息传递。这类电子货币还有相关形式，如“刮刮卡”，即购买附有数字代码的卡以获得电子单位，之后可以用手机消息转移。电信公司也开始允许手机用户将预付话费额度用于与电信无关的各种支付。

Remarkably, the potential for spontaneous money creation represented by technological and institutional changes within financialised capitalism has been more fully apparent in developing countries. E-money proper has come into its own in a swathe of countries in Africa and Asia based particularly on telecommunications enterprises. The spread of mobile telephony has provided the underpinnings of acceptability, and thus ‘moneyness’, for e-money in developing countries. Typically, mobile phone users purchase e-money proper by advancing ordinary money; hold it as electronic units; and transfer it by simple messages. Related forms of e-money include ‘scratch’ cards, that is, electronic units purchased in cards with a code number, which could then be transferred by mobile phone message. Telecommunications companies have also started to allow mobile phone holders to use prepaid airtime units to make a variety of payments unrelated to telephony.
这里的关键是发展中国家的金融制度相对薄弱，特别是其地理覆盖和向经济各领域的渗透都有限，削弱了既有信用货币形式的优势。在发展中国家，开立正规银行账户往往受制于当地没有银行网点、开户成本高昂及最低余额门槛难以达到。此外，在依赖侨汇的低收入国家，通过正规金融渠道汇款的成本可能令人却步。非正式渠道又可能带来显著风险和社会义务。

Vital in this respect has been the relative weakness of financial systems in developing countries, particularly their limited geographical and economic penetration across the economy, which has reduced the strength of incumbent forms of credit money. In developing countries, access to formal bank accounts is often restricted by physical absence of bank branches, high setting-up costs and prohibitive minimum balances. Furthermore, for low-income countries that rely on emigrant remittances, the costs of money transmission through formal financial channels can be prohibitive. Informal mechanisms, on the other hand, could entail significant risks and social obligations.
在这种情况下，严格意义上的电子货币可以作为个人收入和小企业的交换手段与贮藏手段而蓬勃发展。通过手机或“刮刮卡”使用的这类货币，也使低成本向偏远地区汇款成为可能。因此，由私人发行的货币及相关货币创新，使低收入国家有可能绕开正规金融机构，扩大低端的货币流通。

In this context, e-money proper is capable of thriving by acting as means of exchange and hoarding for personal income and for small enterprises. E-money proper based on mobile phones, or ‘scratch cards’, also offers the potential to remit money to remote areas at little cost. Thus, privately issued money and associated monetary innovations have created the possibility of by-passing formal financial institutions in low-income countries and expanding monetary circulation at the lower end.

不同发行者发行的严格意义上的电子货币无法按面值互换，可能妨碍它在发展中国家的进一步普及。一切电子货币都有这个弱点，但当电子货币大范围普及时，该问题就显得更突出。一种电子货币单位只有先兑换为普通货币，才能兑换为另一种电子货币。将来有可能促成彼此兑换，进而扩大严格意义上的电子货币的适用范围。但要做到这一点，就需要引入一套相互清算电子货币负债的制度，给发行者带来显著成本。在发展中国家，这种发展是否可行，尚待观察。

The further spread of e-money proper in developing countries might be hampered by the lack of mutual convertibility of different issues at par. This is a weakness common to all e-money, but its importance becomes more apparent when such money spreads widely. All e-money units have to be converted into ordinary money before they could be turned into each other. It is conceivable that mutual convertibility could be instigated in the future, thus further broadening the range of e-money proper. For this to arise, however, it would be necessary to introduce a system of mutual clearance of e-money liabilities, entailing significant costs for issuers. It remains to be seen whether such a development is feasible in developing countries.

zh: 4.3 金融化高峰时期国家支持的中央银行货币

children: State-Backed Central Bank Money at the Peak of Financialisation
国内无价值货币中，最后一项需要仔细考察的是存放在中央银行的银行准备金。如第3.2节所述，银行准备金是国家支持的信用货币的最重要组成部分，也是国家干预金融领域所依托的支点。下文以图12.10为基础，简要讨论2007年危机前四国银行准备金的变动。考虑到其中涉及的信用过程很复杂，此处的分析所能得出的结论有限。不过，它可以为进一步讨论中央银行业务和国家干预奠定基础。

The final part of domestic valueless money that calls for closer examination comprises bank reserves held with the central banks. Bank reserves, as was mentioned in Section 3.2, are the most important component of state-backed credit money and the pivot of state intervention in the realm of finance. The fluctuations of bank reserves in the four countries during the period preceding the crisis of 2007 are briefly discussed below on the basis of Figure 10. To be sure, only limited analytical mileage can be gained at this point, given the complexity of the credit processes involved. Nonetheless, a basis could be provided for further discussion of central banking and state intervention.
四国银行准备金使用情况有显著差异，最初日本和德国超过另外两国。这些差异反映了各国国内信用体系的组织结构不同，尤其是私人银行与中央银行在货币市场中的互动方式不同。从更根本的层面看，它们揭示了国家对货币领域的干预有所不同。

There have been significant differences in the use of bank reserves among the four countries, Japan and Germany initially surpassing the other two. These differences reflect variations in the institutional structure of the domestic credit system, particularly in the interaction between private banks and the central bank in the money market. But more fundamentally, they reveal differences in state intervention in the monetary sphere.

2001年后，日本银行准备金突然膨胀，这是量化宽松的结果。该政策一方面迫使、另一方面鼓励商业银行积累准备金，希望推动商业放贷。2008—2009年，危机冲击金融部门之际，美国和英国的中央银行也采取了类似政策。2009—2010年，美国银行准备金的相对规模已超过日本的峰值。这意味着美国政策较前一时期有了剧烈变化，此前准备金基本维持在极低水平。在那段时期，美国和英国的银行能够在公开市场上筹措流动资金，贮藏支付手段的意愿也较弱。

The sudden bulging of Japanese bank reserves after 2001 is the outcome of Quantitative Easing, namely the policy of partly forcing, partly encouraging commercial banks to accumulate reserves in the hope of inducing commercial lending. A similar policy was adopted by the us and the uk central banks in 2008–9 as the crisis hit the financial sector. The proportionate size of bank reserves in the usa in 2009–10 has exceeded the peak of the Japanese bulge. This represents a dramatic change from us policy during the preceding period, which basically maintained reserves at very low levels. During that time, banks in the usa and the uk were able to generate liquid funds in open markets; banks were also less inclined to hoard means of payment.

银行准备金对国家干预货币领域历来至关重要，即使其绝对规模较产出和其他形式的货币通常都很小。国家干预货币和金融领域的行动，当然远不限于管理银行准备金，还包括决定利息率等。在金融化时期，国家干预的明确关切，是抑制无价值货币引发通货膨胀、因而无法妥善发挥价值尺度职能的倾向。自20世纪90年代以来，货币政策一直在“中央银行独立”的制度安排中制定，其方针可概括为“通胀目标制”。2000年代的危机给通胀目标制以沉重打击，同时重申了国家能够依托国家支持的中央银行货币干预金融领域。

Bank reserves have been vital to state intervention in the monetary sphere, even when their absolute size has been typically small relative to both output and other forms of money. Needless to say, state intervention in the realm of money and finance is a far broader set of actions than merely managing bank reserves, and includes determination of interest rates. In the years of financialisation, state intervention has been driven by the express concern to limit the propensity of valueless money to generate inflation, and thus to perform inadequately as measure of value. Since the 1990s, monetary policy has been set within the institutional regime of ‘central bank independence’ and has been summed up as ‘inflation targeting’. The crisis of the 2000s has delivered a major blow to inflation targeting, but at the same time reaffirmed the power of the state to intervene in the financial sphere, pivoting on state-backed central bank money.

zh: 5 当代无价值世界货币：作为准世界货币的美元
en: 5 Contemporary Valueless World Money: The Dollar as Quasi-World-Money

children: 布雷顿森林体系瓦解后，信用货币切断了同黄金的联系，这一变化对国际货币领域的冲击比对国内货币领域更大，原因有二。第一，没有一种全球信用体系能够创造出足以替代黄金的国际信用货币。第二，没有一个国家能够在国际层面创造有国家支持的信用货币，从而复制国内普遍采用的货币安排。与由民族国家支撑的国内市场及国家在其中的作用相比，世界市场的结构和主权国家在其中的作用在性质上有别。

The severing of the link of credit money with gold after the collapse of Bretton Woods has had more severe repercussions for the international compared to the domestic monetary sphere for two fundamental reasons. First, there is no global credit system capable of generating a form of international credit money that could adequately operate as replacement for gold. Second, there is no state that could replicate the prevalent domestic monetary arrangements by generating state-backed credit money at the international level. The structure of the world market and the role of sovereign states within it are qualitative different phenomena from that of the domestic market that is supported by the nation state.
实际上，美元已在世界市场中发挥黄金的无价值替代物的作用。不过，这是个问题重重的替代物，造成不稳定且具有剥削性的安排，在金融化资本主义上留下了印记。下文通过简要考察马克思的世界货币理论，探讨这一演变的理论框架。马克思的世界货币理论虽未得到充分发展，却是其货币理论不可分割的一部分。

The us dollar has in practice functioned as a valueless replacement for gold in the world market. But it has been a problematic substitute resulting in unstable and exploitative arrangements that have placed their stamp on financialised capitalism. The theoretical parameters of this development are discussed below by briefly considering Marx’s theory of world money, an undeveloped but integral part of his monetary theory.
马克思在《资本论》第一卷中简要讨论了世界货币这一概念，将之视为“作为货币的货币”的复合职能之一，另两项是贮藏手段和支付手段。
用马克思本人的话说：
Marx discussed the concept of world money briefly in the first volume of
Capital
, treating it as part of the composite function of money ‘as money’ which also comprises means of hoarding and means of payment.
In his own words:
世界货币充当一般支付手段、一般购买手段以及财富本身（一般财富）的绝对社会化身。其主要职能是在结算国际差额时充当支付手段。

World money serves as the universal means of payment, as the universal means of purchase, and as the absolute social materialisation of wealth as such (universal wealth). Its predominant function is as means of payment in the settling of international balances.
这一定义中有几点值得注意。
Several points stand out in this definition.
第一，世界货币具有一切“作为货币的货币”的基本属性，即独立于资本主义的日常流通过程，同时仍能在关键时刻介入，转移价值或结算差额。

First, world money possesses the fundamental attribute of all ‘money as money’, namely to stand aloof from the regular grind of capitalist circulation while remaining capable of intervening decisively to transfer value, or settle balances.
第二，与第一点相关，在世界市场上行动的主体必须持有世界货币，才能在必要时在市场上行动。持有世界货币具有外在强制的成分，超出自由选择的范围。

Second, and related to the first, the agents that operate in the world market are obliged to hold world money to be able to act in the market at required moments; there is an element of external compulsion to holding world money, not merely choice.
第三，也正因如此，持有世界货币是世界市场参与者行使权力的手段。拥有世界货币使他们能在关键时刻支付并转移价值，进而塑造价值创造和流通的基础过程。

Third, by this token, holding world money is an instrument of power for participants in the world market. Its possession affords the opportunity to pay and transfer value at critical junctures thereby shaping the underlying processes of value creation and circulation.
第四，强制和权力共同重申了世界货币的基本“货币性”，也就是它支配商品并在世界市场上成为价值的绝对形式的能力。
Fourth, compulsion and power jointly reaffirm the fundamental ‘moneyness’ of world money, that is, its ability to dominate commodities and to emerge as the absolute form of value in the world market.

“作为货币的货币”的职能是马克思货币理论的特色，使它与古典政治经济学的理论体系有所区别。例如，贮藏职能内在地包含了危机的可能性，因为货币停止购买商品而闲置下来。因此，“作为货币的货币”意味着在理论上有可能与市场自发达到均衡的观念决裂。也因此，古典政治经济学家对货币的贮藏职能感到困扰。以李嘉图为例，他很难承认贮藏货币的重要性，尤其是因为这种贮藏意味着需求可能不足，从而可能发生危机。他和马尔萨斯曾就此展开著名的争论，其中也涉及货币的国际作用。
几十年后，同货币学派争论不休的英国银行学派强调，持有货币可能出于外部强制，例如经济主体有义务必须履行时。

The function of ‘money as money’ is characteristic of Marx’s monetary theory and sets it apart from the corpus of Classical Political Economy. The hoarding function, for instance, inherently contains the possibility of crisis, since money stops buying commodities and lies idle. ‘Money as money’ thus represents a potential theoretical break with the notion of spontaneous market equilibration. Classical Political Economists were, consequently, troubled by money’s hoarding function. Ricardo, for one, could not readily accept the importance of money hoards, particularly because of the implication of insufficient demand and thus crisis. He had a well-known debate with Malthus on this issue, including on the international role of money.

A few decades later, the Banking School in Britain, locked in debate with the Currency School, stressed that there could be external compulsion to holding money as, for instance, when economic agents had obligations to meet.

从这一角度看，马克思强调“作为货币的货币”，显出重商主义对他的影响。在重商主义传统看来，货币远非覆盖在和谐市场上的一层“面纱”，它是财富的体现，能够重塑经济活动，并赋予政治权力。在这方面，重商主义的遗产不仅见于马克思主义，也见于许多非主流货币理论。在分析资本主义危机和流通中断时，非主流理论家往往不得不承认货币的独特作用。就连凯恩斯，在考察两次世界大战之间那场危机的货币现象时，也发现重商主义的某些要素仍然有效。

In this light, Marx’s stress on ‘money as money’ reveals the influence of mercantilism on his thought. For the mercantilist tradition, money was much more than simply a ‘veil’ on harmonious markets, and constituted the embodiment of wealth capable of reshaping economic activity and delivering political power. The legacy of mercantilism in this respect could be found across much heterodox monetary theory, not only Marxism. Heterodox theorists have often been forced to acknowledge the unique role of money when analysing capitalist crises and disruptions of circulation. Even Keynes discovered the continuing validity of elements of mercantilism when he examined the monetary phenomena of the interwar crisis.

马克思货币思想中的重商主义成分在世界货币上表现得最为明显，因为世界货币在世界市场中发挥作用，而世界市场有两个方面不同于国内市场。第一，世界市场没有使各国国内市场趋于同质的法律、约定、惯行和习俗机制。它本来就不如国内市场同质，这也反映了不存在一个可以施加类似国内市场条件的世界国家。世界市场是国际私人资本与民族国家体系相遇的场域。私人资本在世界市场要应对各异的法律、习俗、实际做法乃至文化特点。与此同时，各民族国家必须运用世界市场机制结算差额、转移价值、支付及借款。

The mercantilist strain in Marx’s monetary thought is at its clearest with regard to world money because the latter functions in the world market which differs from national markets in two respects. First, the world market lacks the legal, conventional, practical and customary mechanisms which provide homogeneity to national markets. It is inherently less homogeneous than national markets, also reflecting the absence of a world state that could have imposed conditions analogous to national markets. The world market is the terrain over which international private capitals meet the system of national states. Private capitals have to deal with a range of legal, customary, practical, and even cultural specificities in the world market. At the same time, national states must use the mechanisms of the world market to settle balances, transfer value, make payments, and borrow.
第二，世界市场没有类似各国经济内部信用体系那样的统一信用体系来协调。信用和金融固然渗透了整个世界市场，却未形成由各层次有序信用关系构成的制度，国内制度通常包括商业信用、银行信用和货币市场信用。
由此也就没有可以充当最后贷款人和发行法定清偿手段的世界中央银行。

Second, the world market lacks the coordinating presence of an integrated credit system analogous to the credit system of national economies. Credit and finance certainly permeate the world market, but do not amount to a structured credit system comprising ordered layers of credit relations, typically including commercial, banking and money market credit.
By extension, there is no world central bank that could act as lender of last resort and issuer of legal tender.
基于这些原因，世界货币必须起到协调或组织世界市场的作用，也就是说，必须成为国际资本和各民族国家普遍接受的贮藏手段（储备）和支付手段。要履行这些任务，它也必须充当公认的价值尺度，适用于计量商品和先前形成的义务。最后，它必须有助于国家之间政治和军事权力的行使，体现国家对世界市场的有意识干预。

For these reasons, world money must act as the coordinator or the organiser of the world market, that is, it must be a generally accepted means of hoarding (reserve) and means of payment for both international capitals and national states. In order to deliver these tasks, it must also be a commonly agreed measure of value that could apply to both commodities and past obligations. Finally, it must facilitate the exercise of inter-state political and military power, thus reflecting the conscious intervention of states in the world market.
马克思在《资本论》第三卷第五篇的若干章中，分析了他所处时代的具体货币和商业条件，由此可以看出世界货币作用的复杂性。
简言之，在马克思看来，世界市场会系统性地造成贸易差额失衡，失衡经由危机剧烈地重新调整，迫使世界货币流动。在这一背景下，一国取得世界货币储备的能力，是其全球权力的一个要素。马克思的这一部分论述明显受到重商主义的影响，特别是詹姆斯·斯图亚特爵士的影响。斯图亚特坚持认为，自发的货币流动不会使贸易差额自动归于平衡。
马克思在简要讨论世界货币时，明确赞同斯图亚特所说的“世界的货币”（money of the world）。

The complexity of the role of world money is clear when one turns to Marx’s analysis of the concrete monetary and commercial conditions of his era, found in several chapters of part five of the third volume of
Capital

Briefly put, for Marx, the world market systematically generates disequilibria in the balance of trade, which are violently readjusted through crisis and necessitate forced flows of world money. In this context, the ability of a state to access reserves of world money is an element of global power. There is strong evidence of mercantilist influence on this part of Marx’s work, particularly due to Sir James Steuart, who had insisted that there is no automatic equilibration of trade balances through spontaneous flows of money.
Marx explicitly approved of Steuart’s term ‘money of the world’ in his own brief discussion of world money.
世界货币采取什么形式，是一个复杂问题，与其运作方式联系起来考察时尤其如此。在马克思看来，世界货币采取商品形式，通常是黄金，这再次表明了世界货币本质上的“货币性”。
在国内流通中逐渐被自身无价值的货币排挤到边缘的货币商品，又在世界层面取得了支配地位。黄金在生产中形成的内在价值，是国际价值计量的锚。黄金的储备及流动强制性地为商品和货币资本的国际交易提供秩序。

The form of world money presents complex problems, particularly when taken in conjunction with its functioning. For Marx, world money assumes the commodity form, typically gold, thus reasserting the essential ‘moneyness’ of world money.

The money commodity that is gradually sidelined by valueless forms of money in domestic circulation re-emerges triumphant at the world level. The intrinsic value of gold that is generated in production acts as the anchor of international value measurement. The reserves and flows of gold forcibly provide order to international transactions of commodities and money capital.
遗憾的是，马克思关于世界货币必须采取商品形式的断言未能得到后来的历史支持，同1914年中央银行发行的货币与黄金脱钩的情况不符。在20世纪的大部分时间里，世界货币以各种无价值的非商品形式存在，全部由国家管理。在世界市场上履行货币职能的，通常是在国内创造并以各国政府的法令为基础的信用货币，其中首推美元。这一变化对金融化至关重要。

Unfortunately, Marx’s assertion that world money must take the form of a commodity has not fared well historically, and is at odds with the severing of the link between central-bank-issued money and gold in 1914. For most of the twentieth century, world money has taken a variety of valueless, non-commodity forms, all of which have been managed by the state. The functioning of money in the world market has been typically performed by credit money domestically created and resting on the fiat of national governments, above all, the us dollar. This development is of paramount importance for financialisation.
1944年《布雷顿森林协定》使美元与黄金在一定程度上保持可兑换，但如上所述，二者的联系在20世纪70年代初断裂。此后，国际储备的形成和国际支付（以价值的国际计量为基础）以资本主义史上前所未有的方式依赖国家干预。世界货币更加明显地成为国家权力的工具，特别是世界市场上等级森严的帝国权力的工具。鉴于这些原因，马克思主义文献称当代世界货币为“准世界货币”。

The Bretton Woods Agreement of 1944 maintained a degree of convertibility of the us dollar with gold but, as was noted above, the link was snapped in the early 1970s. Since then, international reserve formation and payments – underpinned by the international measurement of values – have depended on state intervention in ways that are unprecedented in the history of capitalism. World money has become even more clearly an instrument of state power, particularly of hierarchical, imperial power in the world market. For these reasons, contemporary world money has been called ‘quasi-world-money’ in Marxist literature.
美元充当世界货币，给美国带来重大好处，使它得以在国内实施货币政策、维持对外贸易赤字并输入和输出资本。美元的国际使用还推动了发展中国家的金融化，并使价值系统性地转移到美国。不过，主要资本主义强国的国家货币仍在争夺世界货币的职能，尤其是由几个欧洲强国共同创设的特殊世界货币欧元。

The benefits to the usa of the dollar functioning as world money have been substantial in terms of its ability to exercise monetary policy domestically, to maintain foreign trade deficits and to import and export capital. Use of the dollar internationally has also spurred financialisation in developing countries and systematically transferred value to the usa. The function of world money has, however, continued to be contested terrain among the national currencies of the major capitalist powers, not least by the euro, a peculiar form of world money created collectively by several European powers.
